chunks: Yūnus, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muskān, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
"The hadd of the Jew, the Christian, and the slave regarding wine and false accusation is the same. The People of the Covenant were only granted terms that they may drink it in their homes."

He said: And I asked him about the drunken person and the fornicator. He said: "They are to be flogged with whips, stripped, between the shoulders. But as for the hadd in slander, he is flogged over his clothes, with a beating of moderate severity."

key_terms.أَهْلُ الذِّمَّةِ: non-Muslim protected subjects living under covenant
key_terms.الْخَمْرِ: wine or intoxicating drink subject to legal ruling here
key_terms.الْقَذْفِ: the offense of slanderous accusation of unchastity
key_terms.بِالسِّيَاطِ: with whips used in corporal punishment

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about hadd punishments for drinking wine, slander, drunkenness, and zina?
ai.summary: This hadith presents legal rulings concerning hadd punishments for wine-related offenses, slander, drunkenness, and zina. It also states that Ahl al-Dhimmah were only accorded permission to consume wine within their own homes, while clarifying differences in how corporal punishment is carried out for different offenses.
